title: Getting started with saisdata
text: weo one row per country, IMF group countries, year. Net interest column: primary balance minus overall balance. Kenya’s interest bill took 5.4 percent GDP 2025, gross debt 71 percent GDP.
code: weo |>                                   # start with the panel, and then   filter(code == "KEN", year >= 2020) |> # keep Kenya from 2020 on, and then   filter(year <= 2025) |>                # stop at 2025, and then   mutate(                                # add a column:     net_interest = primary_balance - overall_balance # net interest   ) |>                                   # and then   select(year, gross_debt, net_interest) # keep the columns to read #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>    year gross_debt net_interest #>   <int>      <dbl>        <dbl> #> 1  2020       68.0         3.93 #> 2  2021       68.2         4.09 #> 3  2022       67.8         4.37 #> 4  2023       73.4         4.79 #> 5  2024       67.3         5.25 #> 6  2025       71.3         5.45

title: Getting started with saisdata
text: Countries three-letter codes, IMF’s groups . gives typical country’s debt year since 2020.
code: weo |>                                   # start with the panel, and then   filter(str_length(code) == 3) |>       # keep countries, not IMF groups   filter(year >= 2020, year <= 2025) |>  # keep 2020 to 2025, and then   group_by(year) |>                      # make one group per year, and then   summarize(                             # collapse each group to one row:     median_debt = median(gross_debt, na.rm = TRUE) # the middle value   )                                      # close summarize() #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>    year median_debt #>   <int>       <dbl> #> 1  2020        56.8 #> 2  2021        56.2 #> 3  2022        54.4 #> 4  2023        54.4 #> 5  2024        54.1 #> 6  2025        52.9

title: Getting started with saisdata
text: wb_groups joins weo code. gives typical country’s gross debt 2025 income level:
code: weo |>                                  # start with the IMF's panel, and then   filter(year == 2025) |>               # keep 2025, and then   inner_join(wb_groups, by = "code") |> # keep rows found in both, by code   group_by(income_level) |>             # one group per income level, and then   summarize(                            # collapse each group to one row:     countries = n(),                    # how many countries went in     median_debt = median(gross_debt, na.rm = TRUE) # their middle debt   )                                     # close summarize() #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   income_level        countries median_debt #>   <chr>                   <int>       <dbl> #> 1 High income                67        55.7 #> 2 Low income                 24        52.3 #> 3 Lower middle income        47        49.6 #> 4 Upper middle income        58        54.1

title: Getting started with saisdata
text: weo_groups keeps IMF’s layout, years across. Two moves make tidy, give world’s interest bill dollars. two groups’ balances averages weighted GDP, total approximation.
code: bill <- weo_groups |>                             # start with the table, then   select(group_code, indicator, `2001`:`2031`) |> # keep codes and years, then   pivot_longer(                                   # bring the years down:     cols = `2001`:`2031`,                         # every year column     names_to = "year",                            # their names go in year     names_transform = as.integer,                 # as whole numbers     values_to = "value"                           # their numbers go in value   ) |>                                            # and then   pivot_wider(                                    # send the indicators up:     names_from = indicator,                       # one column per indicator     values_from = value                           # filled from value   ) |>                                            # and then   mutate(                                         # add a column:     # primary balance minus overall balance, times GDP, in USD billions     net_interest_usd_bn = (GGXONLB_NGDP - GGXCNL_NGDP) / 100 * NGDPD   ) |>                                            # and then   group_by(year) |>                               # one group per year, then   summarize(                                      # add up the two groups:     net_interest_usd_bn = sum(net_interest_usd_bn) # the world's bill   )                                               # close summarize()  bill |>                               # start with the bill, and then   filter(year %in% c(2001, 2025))     # keep the two years to compare #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>    year net_interest_usd_bn #>   <int>               <dbl> #> 1  2001                849. #> 2  2025               2371.

what: Chart it, and print the credit
title: Getting started with saisdata
text: Every chart made data carries source line. 2026 values IMF projections, chart shades . chart uses World Bank groups, source line drops sentence.
code: bill |>                                           # start with the bill, and then   mutate(                                         # add a column:     kind = if_else(year <= 2025, "Estimate", "IMF projection") # which is which   ) |>                                            # and then   ggplot(aes(x = year, y = net_interest_usd_bn, fill = kind)) + # map columns   geom_col() +                                    # draw one bar a year   scale_fill_manual(                              # choose the two colors:     values = c("Estimate" = "#143E5A", "IMF projection" = "#9CC9D8") # navy, pale   ) +                                             # close scale_fill_manual()   labs(                                           # add the words:     title = "The world's net interest bill is nearly three times its 2001 level",     subtitle = "Net interest of governments, billions of US dollars",     x = NULL,                                     # no x axis title     y = NULL,                                     # no y axis title     fill = NULL,                                  # no legend title     caption = str_c(                              # the source line:       "Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Database, ",       "October 2026,\nhttps://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.RES:WEO. ",       "Net interest is the primary balance\nminus the overall balance, ",       "calculated for this workshop."     )                                             # close str_c()   ) +                                             # close labs()   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +                 # a clean, light theme   theme(                                          # adjust a few details:     legend.position = "top",                      # legend above the chart     panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),           # drop the minor lines     panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),         # drop the vertical lines     plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, color = "grey35"),     plot.title.position = "plot",                 # title at the left edge     plot.caption.position = "plot"                # caption at the left edge   )                                               # close theme()
